paper_metadata.title: Knowledge Graph Population from News Streams
paper_metadata.venue: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, PhD dissertation, Teoria del Senyal i Comunicacions
paper_metadata.abstract: Industrial PhD dissertation on constructing and maintaining media knowledge graphs from online news. It develops multimodal entity linking and type-aware relation extraction; VLX-Stories, an online multilingual event-detection and event-KG system; emerging-entity detection; and SHACL/triple-classification quality controls to populate the Vilynx Knowledge Graph (VKG).

problem_addressed: How to generate a dynamic, high-quality knowledge graph that updates with world changes by extracting entities, relations, events, and novel facts from unstructured, multilingual news streams. The application setting is media-content indexing, search, event exploration, and KG maintenance, where static encyclopedic KGs omit emerging entities and current facts.

methodology.description: The end-to-end workflow is: (1) crawl RSS feeds and parse article text/images; (2) represent articles with NER/POS-derived entities, nouns, and noun chunks, weighted with modified TF-IDF and time; (3) use k-NN tracking and DBSCAN detection to aggregate same-story news; (4) obtain semantic entities through multimodal entity linking, including spaCy NER/POS, visual recognition, OCR, and speech-to-text inputs; (5) dynamically create provisional person 'aspirants' from repeated NIL mentions, then have humans accept, merge as aliases, or reject them; (6) create candidate entity pairs in sentences and use fine-tuned BERT with entity/type markers to classify ontology relations; (7) merge duplicate triples and validate RDF graphs with ontology-derived SHACL type/cardinality/disjoint constraints, exploiting redundancy across an event; (8) aggregate unique triples across events, classify their correctness from 18 redundancy/prediction features, and ingest threshold-passing triples into VKG. Separately, VLX-Stories represents events in an event ontology using who/what/where/when/topic properties.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: VKG is an encyclopedic KG merged from Freebase, Wikidata, and Wikipedia. It supplies entity candidates, an ontology of relation predicates and entity types, and SHACL constraints. The system also defines a VLX-Event Ontology, inspired by journalism's who/what/where/when questions plus topic, category, semantic-pattern entities, and article context. The schema constrains RE outputs and RDF validation.

input_output.input_type: Online multilingual news streams aggregated into same-event article clusters; individual article text and semi-structured metadata, optionally associated images, video/audio transcripts, and OCR text.
input_output.input_granularity: RSS feeds and articles; article titles, descriptions, full text, metadata fields, and sentences; the main KG-population unit is an aggregated-news/event cluster containing multiple articles.
input_output.output_representation: Annotated entities and relation-labelled candidate facts; RDF subject-predicate-object triples and valid RDF subgraphs; populated/updated VKG; and VLX-Stories KG event instances represented by a journalism-W ontology (who, what, where, when, topic, category, article context).

RE: BERTEM entity-marker configuration from Soares et al.; published ERNIE and SpanBERT TACRED results reported for contextual comparison
Triple validation: raw BERTEM+TM RE output ('Base'), then type-only and type+data constraint variants
Triple classification: linear SVM, gradient boosting, random forest, and bagging classifier comparisons
evaluation.setting: The dissertation evaluates modules separately and reports production analytics. RE variants were fine-tuned from BERTBASE for 10 epochs with learning rate 3e-5, Adam, and batch size 64. Triple-classifier data use a 70/30 train/test split. Event clustering used UCI data after URL/keyword/minimum-cluster exclusions, with DBSCAN eps=0.65 and min_samples=5. The paper explicitly notes the absence of a full end-to-end event-system benchmark and the domain shift between Wikipedia-trained RE and news text.

value: Holistic EL: best model F1=0.77 on VLX-News; simulated visual entities raised F1 to 0.82 (5 percentage-point improvement). Human evaluation of 14,024 tags from 1,400 YouTube-8M videos reported 80.87% accuracy.
RE: BERTEM+TM achieved TACRED test P/R/F1=70.3/67.3/68.8 versus BERTEM=67.8/65.3/65.5; on TypeRE it reached P/R/F1/accuracy=90.2/89.5/89.9/93.7 versus BERTEM=87.0/88.3/87.6/92.1.

Event clustering: on the filtered UCI subset, event-detection precision=81.58%; article P/R/F1=94.57/58.54/72.32. Production analytics report 17,296.37 articles/day and 362.48 country-level events/day across seven countries.
Event semantic-pattern linking: 100 patterns yielded P/R/F1/accuracy=0.86/0.94/0.90/0.86.

Emerging entities: recovery of deleted persons was 78.86% across 648 stories. In production, 67.88 emerging entities/day were detected; human review judged 75.45% new entities, 22.15% aliases, and 9.7% NER errors.

RDF validation on AggregatedNewsRE improved precision from 54.5 to 70.1 and F1 from 66.6 to 75.5; recall fell from 85.5 to 81.7. Gradient boosting gave the best triple-classification accuracy (73.8%, ROC AUC=81.0); high-threshold random-forest/bagging runs reportedly achieved about 98% precision with recall above 50%.

In a 24-hour production sample, 88.6% of manually evaluated new triples passing validation were correct. In a daily ingestion run, 57% of 113 unique submitted triples were newly ingested and 84.6% of ingested triples were manually judged correct.

value: REVIEW INFERENCE: The system addresses a complete operational Text-to-KG chain—from stream ingestion and event aggregation through canonical entity/relation extraction, validation, and graph updating—rather than evaluating only an isolated extractor.

REVIEW INFERENCE: Aggregated same-event news provides repeated evidence that the validator and classifier explicitly exploit, and the controlled validation experiment shows a large precision gain with limited recall loss.
REVIEW INFERENCE: Schema-aware methods are used at two points: type markers improve RE and SHACL constraints prevent ontology-incoherent RDF triples.
REVIEW INFERENCE: The 'aspirant' design allows timely provisional tagging and search for emerging persons while retaining human gatekeeping before persistent KG creation.
REVIEW INFERENCE: Evaluation combines public benchmarks, purpose-built datasets, ablations/baselines, and production measurements, making the practical design and trade-offs visible.

These representations work as entities during disambiguation and are indexed by search algorithms. However, they will not be part of the knowledge graph until a human has reviewed and validated it.

value: REVIEW INFERENCE: The pipeline compounds errors across NER, EL, RE, validation, and classification; production analysis identifies erroneous entity disambiguation as the dominant pattern among incorrect ingested triples.
REVIEW INFERENCE: High-precision operating choices deliberately leave many relevant articles/triples unassigned or filtered, constraining coverage and recall.

REVIEW INFERENCE: Several evaluations are custom, small, manually annotated, simulated (deleting known entities), or module-specific; the thesis does not establish an end-to-end benchmark of full KG-population quality.
REVIEW INFERENCE: The system is limited to three languages and production-specific VKG ontology/data infrastructure, so cross-domain and broader multilingual generalization are unproven.
REVIEW INFERENCE: Reliance on human review for final emerging-entity creation improves quality but limits full automation and may delay canonical graph updates.

value: The EL system can produce generic, abstract, and repeated keyword-to-entity mapping errors; unknown/ambiguous contexts remain difficult.
The RE study did not evaluate BERTLARGE because of its high computational requirements.
The news aggregator prioritizes precision and consequently has poor article-assignment recall; business news are especially difficult because financial terms recur across unrelated articles.
Event representation struggles with homonyms and unknown contexts; no suitable end-to-end event-system dataset was available.
Emerging-entity creation is restricted to persons with at least two words; deleted entities can be wrongly linked to same/related aliases.
SHACL type constraints can reject true positives when the KG lacks required entity-type data.
Triple classifiers are limited by annotated-data volume; production errors frequently originate in entity disambiguation.

value: AUTHOR-PROPOSED: Improve EL using more sources/metadata, robustness to noisy and out-of-knowledge-base data, and user-based validation/feedback; add visual-training data and stronger visual recognition.
AUTHOR-PROPOSED: Explore RE architectures that integrate KG information into language-model representations; use BERTLARGE where feasible.
AUTHOR-PROPOSED: Improve false-negative article assignments and design human end-to-end event-quality evaluations.

AUTHOR-PROPOSED: Extend emerging-entity detection beyond people to locations, organizations, and events; automatically identify aliases using multilingual string matching and co-occurrence/context features.
AUTHOR-PROPOSED: Add KG-embedding/context features to triple classification and collect a larger labelled corpus to test neural classifiers.

Future work on this model should focus on adding contextual information thought the use of knowledge graph embeddings... With a larger corpus of triples we would be able to apply neural models.

value: AUTHOR-STATED: Dynamic KG maintenance still needs reliable handling of KG incompleteness, emerging entity canonicalization, aliases, and world changes.
AUTHOR-STATED: Measuring the end-to-end correctness of detected/merged news events remains unresolved without suitable data and human evaluation.
AUTHOR-STATED: The precision–recall trade-off remains unresolved for real-time event tracking and high-quality population.
AUTHOR-STATED: Detecting semantically plausible but factually wrong triples cannot be solved by ontology constraints alone; stronger contextual verification is needed.

REVIEW INFERENCE: Provenance-aware truth assessment, broad multilingual/domain transfer, and fully automated but high-precision entity creation are not demonstrated by this dissertation and remain open for this approach.

code_and_data_availability: The dissertation supplies Figshare URLs for TypeRE and AggregatedNewsRE datasets. It describes production deployment at Vilynx, but does not report a public source-code repository, public trained-model release, public VKG dump, or public full production/news corpus. It cites the public YouTube-8M, TACRED, and UCI-ML News Aggregator resources used in evaluations.
